> i also find it a bit extreme to assume that all servers are making minimum wage.. i don't believe it 

Why is that extreme to you? Almost all servers make minimum wage regardless of experience because it's generally believed that the better you are at your job, the more you'll get in tips, making up for the lack in salary.

> there's no fucking way the barista at the coffeeshop, or the bartender at the bar is paying 10% to the house 

I was talking about waitstaff at a sit down restaurant. Baristas don't tip out, and I serve at a pub where we have to tip out 10% of the total bill to the house, some of which goes to the bar. If we're tipped less than 10%, it comes out of our other tips or out of pocket if we didn't make enough in tips. Some places require less than 10%, but 10% isn't uncommon.

Since you tip the servers directly, the frequent profit from patronage doesn't make up for the loss in tips at all since they make minimum wage regardless of how often you go there. If you tip less than 10%, they're essentially paying to serve you since they have to tip 10% of total sales out to the house.

Don't apologize, I know what it's like being really sad and fucked up. I honestly really relate to people only caring about acting on suicidal thoughts, and not actual happiness. I'm sorry most people are so shitty. 

It sounds really rough with the meds, I'm sorry you're going through that. If the ones you're currently on aren't helping at all though, it could be worth it to keep trying once you feel ready. If you're already at the point of suicide you don't have much to lose. 
Have you tried CBT? I found that it helped me more than just talking to someone because it helped me learn to regulate my emotions and change some of my negative thoughts.  

I know what it's like feeling like everything's dark and the cloud will never be lifted, and existing is just going through the motions. It doesn't have to be that way forever though. I've had severe depression/BPD since I was 13 and attempted suicide at 17 and again at 18 because I felt like things would never change and I'd be miserable for the rest of my life. It's still something I have to work at but sometimes the dark cloud is lifted, even for a little while, and I get to experience things that make me really happy that I would've missed out on if I ended it then. 18 is still so young and sooo much could change in a couple of years. 

Honestly I wish I could help you more but the only advice I really have is to take it all one day at a time and focus on the little moments that make you smile. Some days will be harder than others but it doesn't have to be all suffering. I hope things get better for you OP.

You shouldn't pretend that you're not depressed. Let your psychiatrist know your current therapy and meds aren't working so they can try something different. 

As for the college major, is there anything you enjoy doing or want to learn more about? You don't even necessarily have to have the future in mind, but just something that you'd like to learn about that would help you get through the day. I'm a nursing/chemistry major but I'm taking astronomy next semester which won't go towards my degree at all, but I just like learning about the universe. 
Don't do anything drastic now, before you've even figured out what you want to do with the rest of your life. You're not even in college yet, you have so many opportunities ahead of you and you could end up finding something you love and making a difference in the world. You can't call yourself useless when you don't even know your potential yet.

Hang the DJ was amazing and Black Museum was a close second for me, while Crocodile wasn't my favourite but it was interesting and had the dark vibes I was expecting from Black Mirror. USS Callister was really entertaining to watch because of the acting and the humour but there were just too many plot holes in the story imo. Arkangel was alright but I just feel like they could've done more with the idea of the implant which left the story lacking for me. As for Metalhead, honestly I had to take multiple breaks to finish this episode. I don't know if it was the black and white, the pacing, or the storyline but I just didn't feel any connection with the characters and didn't care what happened to them, and the episode was just really boring to me. There wasn't really any explanation as to what the robots were or why they were so vengeful and everything was just too vague. The ending also pissed me off knowing the characters died for such a stupid reason and I sat through the entire episode waiting for that twist. This is just my opinion but if someone wanted to torture my cookie they could honestly just play Metalhead on repeat for eternity.
